title: Pastéis de Nata
description: Custard tarts baked in the hottest oven you have, so the tops blister black while the centre stays loose. The pastry is rolled into a log and cut, not lined.
notes: Makes 12. Domestic ovens rarely reach the 300°C these want; go as hot as yours goes and put the tray on the floor of the oven.

steps.text: Boil the sugar and water with the cinnamon stick and lemon peel to a thin syrup, then set it aside to infuse.
Whisk the flour into a little of the cold milk to a smooth slurry, then stir in the rest of the milk and cook until thickened.
steps.tip: Lumps here cannot be fixed later. Slurry first, always.

steps.text: Strain the warm syrup into the hot milk mixture in a steady stream, whisking.
Let it cool below blood heat, then whisk in the egg yolks and strain the custard.
steps.tip: Yolks into anything hotter than this scramble instantly.

steps.text: Roll the puff pastry into a tight log, cut it into 12 discs, and press each cut-side-down into a muffin tin, thumbing it up the sides.
steps.tip: Cut side down is what gives the layered spiral on the base.

steps.text: Chill the cases while the oven heats as high as it will go.
Fill each case three-quarters full and bake until the tops are blistered and blackened in patches.
steps.temperature: as hot as the oven goes
steps.tip: The black spots are correct. Pale tarts are underbaked.

steps.text: Cool briefly and eat warm, dusted with cinnamon.
